INTERNAL RATINGS-BASED (IRB) MODEL DOCUMENTATION
Credit Risk Models — Version 2.1

1. SCOPE AND OVERVIEW

This document covers the internal model approach for credit risk under the IRB framework
as implemented by the institution. The IRB approach is applied to retail and corporate
exposures. Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), and Exposure at
Default (EAD) estimates are produced by internal models and used in regulatory capital
calculations.

2. GOVERNANCE AND INTERNAL VALIDATION

The model development team is organizationally separate from the risk validation unit.
The validation function reports to the Chief Risk Officer and has independent budget
authority. Validation activities are documented in validation reports reviewed by the
Model Risk Committee quarterly.

Internal audit reviews the IRB framework annually. Audit findings are tracked and
remediation timelines are agreed with model owners. The last audit found no critical
deficiencies in the PD models.

3. DATA GOVERNANCE

Historical data covering at least 5 years of default observations is maintained in the
model data warehouse. Data quality checks are performed monthly including completeness,
accuracy, and consistency checks. Reference data sets are versioned and frozen at each
calibration cycle.

The institution uses both internal data and pooled external data from a consortium for
low-default portfolios. Data representativeness is assessed annually.

4. PD MODEL — CORPORATE EXPOSURES

The PD model for corporate exposures uses a logistic regression framework with
financial ratio inputs: leverage ratio, interest coverage, profitability, and liquidity.
Ratings are mapped to one-year PD estimates via a calibration curve. The calibration
is validated annually against observed default rates over a 10-year reference period.

Long-run average default rates are computed as simple averages across economic cycles.
Downturn adjustments are applied where the long-run average is below the through-the-cycle
estimate. MoC (Margin of Conservatism) is added to account for data limitations.

5. LGD ESTIMATION

LGD estimates are based on workout recoveries from resolved defaults in the institution's
history. Downturn LGD is calibrated using an economic indicator approach aligned with the
institution's historical loss experience during the 2008-2010 downturn period.

Collateral haircuts are applied based on forced-sale value estimates. LGD for unsecured
exposures is set at the observed average for the relevant portfolio segment.

6. EAD AND CONVERSION FACTORS

Conversion factors (CF) for revolving credit facilities are estimated from internal data.
The reference data set covers 7 years of drawdown observations prior to default events.
CFs are validated against out-of-sample data each calibration year.

7. MODEL USE AND INTEGRATION

IRB estimates are used in ICAAP, pricing, provisioning, and limit-setting processes.
The use test is documented and evidenced through management reporting packs that include
PD-banded portfolio views presented to the Credit Committee monthly.

8. CHANGE MANAGEMENT

Material changes to models are subject to the Model Change Policy. Changes are classified
as major, moderate, or minor. Major changes require pre-implementation validation and
regulatory notification. A model change register is maintained with details of all changes
since initial approval.

9. REVIEW AND BACKTESTING

Annual performance reviews cover discriminatory power (Gini, AUC), calibration (Hosmer-
Lemeshow test, traffic light approach), and stability (Population Stability Index). Results
are documented in annual model performance reports submitted to the Model Risk Committee.

Backtesting of PD estimates uses the traffic light approach per EBA guidelines with
amber and red triggers leading to management actions.

10. RETURN TO NON-DEFAULTED STATUS

The institution applies a 3-month probation period before an obligor may return to
non-defaulted status. Re-default rates are monitored annually.
